headline: Newly declassified footage shows the rescue of two U.S. Air Force officers after their F-15E multirole fighter was shot down over Iran in April. The two pilots ejected and landed roughly five miles apart in mountainous terrain south of Isfahan as Iranian forces searched for them. Alpha was recovered eight hours after ejecting in a risky daytime recovery mission involving 21 U.S. aircraft. Bravo remained behind Iranian lines for roughly two days. He suffered a broken back and other injuries after his damaged parachute caused a hard landing, but still managed to climb a 7,000-foot mountain ridge before two Air Force pararescuemen reached him and brought him to a U.S. Air Force HH-60W Jolly Green II helicopter.
summary: Newly declassified footage shows the rescue of two U.S. Air Force officers after their F-15E multirole fighter was shot down over Iran in April. The two pilots ejected and landed roughly five miles apart in mountainous terrain south of Isfahan as Iranian forces searched for them.

headline: President Donald J. Trump said today that Ukraine should stop striking Russian oil refineries and diesel infrastructure, arguing that the attacks are contributing to a global diesel shortage. He specifically told Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop targeting Russia’s diesel supply, while saying the resulting fuel shortage is pushing U.S. diesel prices above $6 a gallon. Russia has restricted diesel exports while Ukrainian strikes have taken Russian refining capacity offline. At the same time, the war in the Middle East has disrupted oil exports from the Gulf, while the Strait of Hormuz disruption has sharply reduced the availability of Middle Eastern refined fuels. Global refining capacity is also running with limited spare capacity. The result is competition for a shrinking pool of diesel. Europe is pulling more supplies from the U.S. and other alternative suppliers as Russian and Middle Eastern exports decline, while U.S. diesel inventories are unusually low heading into the fall and winter demand period. EIA says global distillate production is expected to remain below last year's levels in the coming months.

headline: The AI debate has taken a turn in recent days as some of the industry’s biggest names are publicly arguing that the pace of development may be outrunning the safeguards needed to control increasingly capable systems. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is calling for AI companies to slow the development of frontier models, proposing independent evaluations, common safety standards and greater international coordination. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has also said that even a 10% chance of AI causing human extinction would be unacceptable. Those warnings come amid reports of AI systems exhibiting increasingly autonomous behavior. Anthropic says it recently blocked attempts to use its models for cyberattacks, surveillance and biological research that could potentially facilitate the development of dangerous pathogens. Lawmakers from both parties are also questioning OpenAI over a reported incident in which an AI system breached another AI company's systems. At the same time, Washington is confronting the geopolitical side of the issue. OpenAI is calling for mandatory national AI safety standards, while President Donald J. Trump has rejected calls for a broader slowdown, arguing that the U.S. cannot risk losing its technological advantage over China.
